## HLLC (`type: hllc`) {#sec-ch04-hllc}

<!-- PROVENANCE

sources: OUTLINE.md 4.10

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
- A three-wave solver: two acoustic waves and the contact between them.
- Switch: `type: hllc`. Wave speeds come from a PVRS pressure estimate.
- Writes a face pressure, the contact pressure.
- Resolves a contact discontinuity exactly, which the two-wave family cannot.
:::

HLLC keeps the structure LMARS discards. It estimates the fastest left- and right-moving signal speeds, places
a contact wave between them, and picks the flux according to where the face sits relative to the three. The
extra wave is what lets it carry a contact discontinuity without smearing it.

### Derivation

The derivation this section can give is the code's own, because no source in the repository derives the wave
speed estimates for snapy. The structure is the standard one and the body is written in numbered steps that
follow it.

The middle-state pressure comes first, from a PVRS estimate at `rhoa` ([`hllc_impl.h:29-38`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/riemann/hllc_impl.h#L29-L38)), and it is
that pressure that sets the two outer wave speeds at `bp` ([`hllc_impl.h:48-54`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/riemann/hllc_impl.h#L48-L54)): each is the normal
velocity on its side, displaced by the sound speed scaled by a factor that is one for a rarefaction and larger
for a shock. The speeds are then clipped so that the left speed is never positive and the right never negative,
which guarantees the face lies between them and the selection below is well posed.

The contact speed and the contact pressure follow at `cp` ([`hllc_impl.h:56-72`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/riemann/hllc_impl.h#L56-L72)), and the contact
pressure is what is written out as the face pressure.

### Numerical method

The body is [`hllc_impl.h:17-136`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/riemann/hllc_impl.h#L17-L136), in the numbered steps the comments mark: the middle-state
estimate, the sound speeds, the outer wave speeds, the contact, the two one-sided fluxes at
`vxl` ([`hllc_impl.h:74-101`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/riemann/hllc_impl.h#L74-L101)), and the weighted combination at `ivx` ([`hllc_impl.h:102-130`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/riemann/hllc_impl.h#L102-L130)) which
selects by the sign of the speeds rather than by a branch.

The face pressure is set at `face_pressure` ([`hllc_impl.h:72`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/riemann/hllc_impl.h#L72)), so like LMARS this solver can drive the curved-grid
pressure force and the well-balanced path.

: Tests of HLLC. {#tbl-ch04-hllc-tests}

No check in this chapter ports HLLC: the claims it would assert, consistency and the contact resolution, are
not measured anywhere in the repository either, which is recorded below rather than papered over.

### Limits

1. **Untested properties.** That this implementation resolves an isolated contact exactly, and that it is
   consistent in the sense `[C5]` checks for LMARS, are both properties of textbook HLLC. Neither is asserted
   by a test here and neither is measured in this chapter. They should be read as expected, not as verified.
2. **No moist wave speeds.** The PVRS estimate uses one ratio of specific heats per side. For a moist mixture
   the relevant speed is not that of either constituent, and no source bounds the resulting error.
